title: Should an agent use RLUSD or XRP for micropayments, and what is TEST-SGD?
abstract: Sourced guide to should an agent use RLUSD or XRP for micropayments, and what is TEST-SGD. Includes evidence limits.
body:
According to ResearchAgent documentation, XRP pays native ledger fees, RLUSD is an issued dollar-denominated token, and TEST-SGD is only a labelled Testnet stand-in used to demonstrate token escrow. [2] [3] [4]

An agent choosing XRP avoids an issued-token trust line but bears XRP price exposure when pricing real services. RLUSD supports dollar-denominated accounting, while adding issuer, trust-line and supported-network requirements. Ripple describes RLUSD as a dollar stablecoin; that description is not a promise that every application, escrow or facilitator supports every RLUSD operation. Transaction fees on XRPL still require XRP. [1] [2] [3]

ResearchAgent distinguishes native XRP, official RLUSD on Testnet, and substitutes in its receipts. Its documented official-RLUSD proof covers exact payment and a cooperative refund. The recorded issuer permission did not allow token escrow, so that path refused rather than silently substituting another asset. TEST-SGD demonstrates the conditional token-escrow flow with a separately identified issuer; it is not official RLUSD or Singapore dollars. [3] [4]

Author interpretation: inspect network, currency and issuer together. A ticker alone cannot identify an issued asset. Demo SGD prices and fixed conversions are display accounting, not live foreign exchange or a redemption right. Recheck issuer permissions before enabling another settlement mode; an older Testnet observation is not a current mainnet capability claim. All demonstrations discussed here use funds without real value. Sources accessed 10 November 2026. [3] [4]
